I grow cassava and maize together on this sandy plot because that is what feeds my family and brings some money at the market. The soil here is weak, so I always spread manure first, and this season I still have half a bag of urea from the voucher program that I will put on the maize. I keep my own seed from last harvest — it is hardy and I trust it. We will work the land with hoes, my wife and children and I, and I will pay a few young men from the village to help when the weeds are thick and at harvest time.
